title: Tame torsor ramification is killed by the group-order root over a DVR
statement: Let B be a discrete valuation ring (a nonfield local principal ideal domain) with uniformizer pi, K=Frac(B), a finite group G of order n invertible in B, and a finite etale G-torsor T->Spec K [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]. Set A=B[t]/(t^n-pi), q:Spec A->Spec B, j:Spec K->Spec B, and a=pullback.snd(T.pi followed by j,q). Assume a quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and its relative normalization [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization] finite over Spec A. At any point x of this normalization lying over (t), the maximal ideal of its stalk is generated by the structural image of the explicit root t. This is only the index-one calculation over a DVR; there is no ambient chart, arbitrary Noetherian H, or assertion of nonmembership in the square.

proof.text: The order n is positive. For n=1 the root ring is B; for n>=2 Tag 09EV identifies A with a DVR whose uniformizer is t and whose ramification index over B is n. Its fraction field is K(pi^(1/n)). The quotient A/(t)=B/(pi) also identifies the root prime and closed point.

Apply finite etale field Galois classification. Choose a geometric point of T and identify its geometric points with G using the torsor action. Absolute Galois automorphisms commute with this left action, so they act by right multiplication through a finite image subgroup J of G. The stabilizer is the kernel of this homomorphism and is normal; each orbit therefore corresponds to a Galois field extension with Galois group J. Its degree is |J|, which divides n. Tag 09EB gives degree = number of primes times ramification index e times residue degree f. Hence e and f divide n. In positive residue characteristic p, the inseparable residue degree is a p-power dividing f, while p does not divide n. It is therefore one, and e is prime to p. In characteristic zero residue extensions are automatically separable. Every field factor is tame.

Apply 0BRM to each tame DVR extension and the root-field extension. The old ramification index divides n, the new base index. Thus all normalized tensor-product field factors are formally smooth in the maximal-ideal topology. Tag 09E7 makes their ramification indices one. The image of the root uniformizer consequently generates each maximal ideal. The affine relative normalization is integral closure in the finite generic algebra; localization of integral closure (0307) identifies its stalks with these local factors and preserves the structural image of t. This yields the displayed ideal equality, factor by factor, including disconnected torsors.

lean.statement:
theorem dvr_root_normalization_maximalIdeal
    (B : CommRingCat.{u}) [IsDomain B] [IsDiscreteValuationRing B]
    (pi : B) (hpi : Irreducible pi)
    (G : Type (u + 1)) [Group G] [Finite G]
    (T : GaloisCover G (Spec (CommRingCat.of (FractionRing B))))
    (hn : IsUnit (Nat.card G : B)) :
    let A := AdjoinRoot ((Polynomial.X : Polynomial B) ^ Nat.card G - Polynomial.C pi)
    let N := Spec (CommRingCat.of A)
    let q := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap B A))
    let j := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap B (FractionRing B)))
    let a := pullback.snd (T.π ≫ j) q
    ∀ (hqc : QuasiCompact a) (hqs : QuasiSeparated a),
    letI := hqc
    letI := hqs
    IsFinite a.fromNormalization →
    ∀ (x : a.normalization),
      (a.fromNormalization x).asIdeal = Ideal.span
        {AdjoinRoot.root ((Polynomial.X : Polynomial B) ^ Nat.card G - Polynomial.C pi)} →
      let C := a.normalization.presheaf.stalk x
      let tau := (a.fromNormalization.stalkMap x).hom
        (AlgebraicGeometry.StructureSheaf.toStalk A (a.fromNormalization x)
          (AdjoinRoot.root ((Polynomial.X : Polynomial B) ^ Nat.card G - Polynomial.C pi)))
      IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal C = Ideal.span {tau}
